site.page_title: Thrive 360 — Hire for judgment, not a résumé
site.meta_description: Thrive 360 places young adults on real work, documents how they perform, and hands employers evidence before the interview.
site.og_title: You're hiring for judgment. But nobody's teaching that anymore.
site.og_description: Entry-level work used to build judgment. It got automated. Thrive 360 gives you the record instead.

hero.lede_1: Entry-level work used to teach judgment. A vendor call, a deadline that moved, a small thing you owned until it was done. That work is now software. New hires arrive with a degree and no scar tissue.
hero.lede_2: Thrive 360 places young adults on real work with real consequences, documents how they handle it, and hands you the record before you interview.
hero.image_alt: A candidate portfolio page showing scored evidence across seven dimensions
hero.caption: Every candidate arrives with a record, not a promise

problem.heading: Three résumés, three interviews, and you still don't know.
problem.kicker: Hiring at the entry level is a guess dressed up as a process. Everyone in the room knows it. Almost nobody says it out loud.

cards.title: Anyone can say they're reliable
cards.body: The document describes who someone believes they are, edited by whoever coached them. It says nothing about what happened when the deadline moved.

cards.title: Confidence is not competence
cards.body: The best talker in the room is regularly the worst hire. The person who would quietly own the work gets filtered out before anyone finds out.

cards.title: The first rung got automated
cards.body: The filing, the follow-up, the small accountability that built judgment in previous generations is now software. The scar tissue never forms.

get.heading: Evidence instead of a hunch.
get.kicker: We don't send you a candidate and hope. We send you a person plus the record of what they did, how they handled being wrong, and whether the people around them got better.

cards.title: A portfolio, not a résumé
cards.body: Completed assignments, the brief they were given, what they actually delivered, and what their team lead wrote about working with them.

cards.title: A rubric you can defend
cards.body: The same seven dimensions scored the same way for every candidate, with a written right to challenge an assessment they think is wrong.

cards.tag: On the job, in our shop
cards.title: A ninety-day track record
cards.body: They've been accountable to real deadlines with real people counting on them, before they ever cost you a bad quarter.

measure.heading: Seven dimensions, scored on behaviour.
measure.kicker: Not a personality test and not a self-assessment. Every score comes from something the candidate did in front of other people, plus feedback from the people who worked beside them.

dims.title: Character
dims.body: Honesty, fairness, how they handle being wrong

dims.title: Caring
dims.body: Respect and empathy for the people around them

dims.title: Courage
dims.body: Willingness to make the difficult decision

dims.title: Humility
dims.body: Ability to hear feedback and move on it

dims.title: Accountability
dims.body: Follow-through and ownership of the result

how.heading: A small cohort, run properly, before you commit to anything.

steps.title: You tell us the work
steps.body: The real tasks you struggle to fill or can't get to. Not a job description — the actual work.

steps.title: We place a candidate on it
steps.body: Young adults from the local area, matched to the work and to a mentor who has done it before.

steps.title: We observe and document
steps.body: Ninety days of assignments with increasing responsibility, scored on the seven dimensions as they go.

steps.title: You interview with evidence
steps.body: You see the portfolio first. If it isn't persuasive, you've spent nothing but the conversation.

how.note: Honest about the stage we're at: this is a first cohort of ten to fifteen people across a handful of local initiatives, not a national program with a brochure. Employers working with us now are shaping what the record actually contains.

ecosystem.heading: They're already doing the work — for a cause they chose.
ecosystem.kicker: Thrive runs specific local initiatives: conservation, elections, land use, education, family, health, governance. People join because they care about one of them. The work is real, the accountability is real, and the record we hand you comes out of it.
ecosystem.image_alt: Thrive ecosystem: nature, elections, candidates, land use, education, family, health, governance

young.heading: Nobody has asked you what you actually want. We will.
young.kicker: A real conversation, not a form. Then one piece of work that's genuinely yours, a mentor who has done it before, and a record of what you can do that follows you when you go for the job. You don't need a résumé to start.
young.image_alt: A young adult working on a real assignment with a mentor

channels.heading: Where we post.

final.body: One conversation about the work you're trying to fill. We'll show you the record we're building and you can judge whether it beats a résumé.
